posts.author: elonmusk
posts.text:
Let’s take this gentleman’s argument at face value that anyone can throw money at rockets and get something like Starship, Falcon or Dragon.

Perhaps he can explain to everyone how SpaceX is able to catch giant starships from orbit with chopsticks and deliver 85% of all Earth payload to orbit with Falcon, while Blue Origin, which started before SpaceX and was funded by the immensely wealthy Jeff Bezos, is not yet able to launch reliably?

Also, why is it that Boeing and Lockheed received several times what SpaceX did from the government for development of their rockets and spacecraft, but the Boeing capsule is still not operational and ULA delivers less than 5% of SpaceX payload to orbit?

I am genuinely curious about these questions.

BREAKING: Dominican Republic Government advances plans to expand Starlink connectivity and explores Grok for education. 🇩🇴

President Luis Abinader met with SpaceX executives and the Instituto Tecnológico de las Américas (ITLA) to discuss the initiatives:

• More than 50,000 Starlink antennas are already installed across the country.

• Starlink is already benefiting 1,608 students at ITLA’s Pedernales and Cotuí campuses.

• Further expansion would bring internet to communities and schools where traditional services are limited or unavailable.

• Grok Tutor is being considered for personalized learning support, helping students develop reasoning and critical thinking with teacher supervision.

• Its potential integration would support RD Inteligente, a Government program aiming to train one million Dominicans in AI.

BREAKING: Greece’s government is using Starlink to support a railway safety system that warns of potential train collisions. 

Starlink sends live train data to the control center, including through mountainous areas without mobile coverage.

• Monitoring equipment installed on 134 locomotives.
• GNSS-HEPOS positioning pinpoints trains with accuracy of up to 5 centimeters.
• Location updates every second.
• A 24/7 control center receives automatic collision-risk alerts so operators can intervene.

Starlink is now pulling travelers away from competing airlines

United Airlines CEO Scott Kirby:

Kirby calls Starlink “a really unique RASM tailwind” for the airline

Inflight Wi-Fi used to be something travelers complained about

Now it's becoming a reason to switch airlines entirely

Starlink is changing the economics of airline competition

BREAKING: Samsung reportedly plans to make chips for SpaceX’s Starlink satellites in Austin, Texas. 

Samsung is investing $1.9 billion to expand its Austin chip factory, with the planned operations targeted to begin by 2030, according to Seoul Economic Daily.

The chip, called STM32V8, is already used in Starlink’s mini laser system. SpaceX’s Starlink engineering team has praised the chip’s performance.

The chips are currently manufactured in France. The reported Texas plan would add American production capacity for a key component behind Starlink’s satellite communications.

BREAKING: Former White House and Pentagon official Douglas MacKinnon calls for an end to political attacks on Elon Musk, saying “our very survival may depend on him.”

• Humanity’s future is vulnerable as long as we live on only one planet. War, an asteroid strike or another major disaster could threaten civilization.

• Elon’s mission is to help humans live on other planets, giving future generations a better chance of surviving if disaster strikes Earth.

• His work toward a permanent human presence in space could become one of his most important contributions to humanity.

• People can disagree with his politics and still recognize the value of what he is trying to achieve.

• MacKinnon argues that Elon deserves the time and freedom to focus on this mission.

Elon is working toward a future where humanity can live beyond Earth and explore the stars. His determination to make that possible deserves recognition and support.

SpaceX is preparing for its 15th Starship launch from South Texas, with spectators gathering just across the street from the 400-foot rocket ahead of Friday’s planned test flight.

The test is a key step in SpaceX’s goal of making Starship fully reusable for future missions, including expanding its Starlink network and eventually carrying astronauts to the Moon and Mars, @JasonAllenLive reports.
